**Marcus Cornelius Fronto** (c. 100 – late 160s AD), best known as **Fronto**, was a Roman grammarian, rhetorician, and advocate. Of [Berber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berbers) origin, he was born at [Cirta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirta) (modern-day [Constantine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constantine,_Algeria), [Algeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algeria)) in [Numidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Numidia). He was [suffect consul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_consul) for the [*nundinium*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nundinium) of July–August 142 with [Gaius Laberius Priscus](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaius%20Laberius%20Priscus) as his colleague.[1] Emperor [Antoninus Pius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antoninus_Pius) appointed him tutor to his adopted sons, the future emperors [Marcus Aurelius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Aurelius) and [Lucius Verus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucius_Verus).
